subject: Post-demo: inference scale & dedicated sizing follow-up
messages:

Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@acme-retail.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Subject: Post-demo: inference scale & deployment questions

Thanks again for the demo today — the team found the latency and multi-tenant routing features compelling. A few items we wanted to capture from our side so you can size options: 

- Peak TPS target: ~200 requests/sec during promotional spikes (sustained baseline ~40 TPS).
- Average prompt length: ~120 tokens; 95th percentile prompt length ~1,800 tokens (we have some long-context retrieval use cases).
- Typical response length: 40-80 tokens.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 200ms for short prompts (<=256 tokens); longer contexts are more tolerant (<=1s).
- Security: we need VPC deployment or dedicated instances; SOC 2 evidence attached (security_q1.pdf).
- Procurement: expect a vendor decision by end of December; procurement will want a quote for Dedicated reserved capacity + a Private VPC option.

Attached is a sampled traffic export (prod_traffic_sample.csv) with representative timestamps and size columns. Happy to set up a technical follow-up — Raj and I are available next week.

Thanks,
Emily
Head of Search & Personalization
Acme Retail
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: inference scale & deployment questions

Emily — thanks for the clear notes and the sample. High level recap / next steps below so we align before the technical sizing call: 

Recap of requirements you called out:
- Peak ~200 TPS (40 baseline / 200 spike)
- Prompt distribution: median ~120 tokens, heavy tail up to ~1,800 tokens
- p95 latency target 200ms for short requests
- Preference for dedicated or VPC-hosted deployment for compliance
- Procurement timeline: decision by EoDec

A couple quick clarifying questions to size Dedicated properly (if you can confirm before our follow-up call it will speed the estimate):
1) For the long-tail 1,800-token prompts, are the long contexts mostly retrieval + short generation (e.g., 40–80 token outputs) or long-generated outputs?
2) Do you expect streaming token-by-token responses in production or do you prefer chunked responses (complete response per request)?
3) What percent of traffic is latency-sensitive vs batchable (can tolerate 500ms+ to allow batching)?
4) Any preference on GPU family? We typically recommend H100 for large models >= 70B and A100 for quantized 30B-class models; we can show cost/latency tradeoffs.

Proposed next steps:
- Karthik to run a quick model/hardware mapping against your sample (we'll need a tokenized sample if possible).
- Diego to prepare two initial sizing options: (a) Dedicated reserved baseline sized for 40 TPS with 200% burst to 200 TPS; (b) Private VPC configuration with similar sizing and network notes.
- Technical deep-dive (30–45m) next Tue/Wed — propose Tue 11/24 10:00am ET.

I copied Laura (solutions lead) to scope any console/SLA/business questions.

Cheers,
Diego Fernandez
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: inference scale & deployment questions

Emily / Diego — I pulled the sample and sketched out preliminary throughput estimates across typical model families. Assumptions: tokenization matches your CSV samples, model flavors below represent a reasonable starting point for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) patterns where output length is ~60 tokens: 

Estimates (very coarse — will refine after tokenized sample):
- 30B quantized (INT8 / A100) => ~12–18 TPS per GPU at p95 for 120-token prompts; long-context handling reduces TPS to ~4–6 for 1800-token prompts.
- 70B (mixed precision / H100) => ~6–10 TPS per GPU for 120-token prompts; ~2–3 TPS for 1800-token prompts.
- 13B distilled (A100) => ~25–40 TPS per GPU for short prompts; better for latency-sensitive bursty workloads but may trade off quality on certain tasks.

Sizing sketch for meeting your 200 TPS spike target (targeting latency SLO for short prompts):
- If short-prompt traffic dominates (>=80%): 5x A100 (30B quantized) nodes anticipated to hit ~200 TPS with headroom for bursts; streaming enabled.
- If long-context traffic (>=20%) is significant: recommend 4x H100-backed nodes running a 70B variant plus a dedicated long-context pool (1–2 nodes) to offload 1.8k-token requests — this improves p95 for short requests by isolating long runs.

Operational notes:
- Concurrency settings: 64 concurrent requests per A100 GPU is a practical starting point for short prompts; for H100 we recommend lower concurrency (16–32) when using fp16 / bf16.
- KV/prefix caching: we can enable a prefix cache for repeated retrieval hits which can reduce compute for long-context RAG cases.
- Autoscale/burst policy: configure baseline reserved pool + burst pool (pay-as-you-go) to cover marketing spikes — this keeps committed costs lower while meeting spikes.

I'll bring concrete GPU-hours and cost estimates to the technical deep-dive once we have the tokenized sample. If useful I can also prepare an alternate configuration that favors lower-cost A100-only fleet but larger cluster size.

-Karthik
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Diego / Karthik — thanks for the clear breakdown. A few quick items from procurement/ops: 

- We'll upload the tokenized sample by EOD Monday (pointing at the CSV you referenced).
- We have a strong preference for Dedicated reserved capacity (we want control over data residency and predictable performance); Private VPC is acceptable if the cost delta isn't material.
- For the long-context flows, they are primarily retrieval + short generation (~60 tokens) rather than long generated sequences.
- Streaming is preferred for UX.
- Procurement want a simple one-pager quote for Dedicated (3 options: A100-optimized, H100-optimized, Hybrid) and an estimated lead time for Private VPC deployment.

We can do the technical deep-dive Tue 11/24 10am ET. Please include estimated monthly committed cost ranges and a short note on fallback model routing for capacity constrained periods.

Cheers,
Raj Patel
Director, ML Infrastructure
Acme Retail
